paper_title: What Does Neuro Mean to Cardio Investigating the Role of Clinical   Specialty Data in Medical LLMs
caption_used: Negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens between baseline MistralV0.2-Base and the same model further fine-tuned on each specialty data. The chart displays six specialty groups along the x-axis (Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, Pediatrics), with the y-axis showing negative log probability ranging from approximately -27 to -22. Within each group, the MistralV0.2-Base bar (light blue) consistently shows the highest negative log probability, indicating weaker token predictions at baseline. Among the fine-tuned models, the Gastro-tuned variant achieves the lowest negative log probability across most specialty groups, suggesting strong cross-specialty transfer. Notably, the Infect group shows the largest overall bar heights, with baseline reaching approximately -23.5, while the Cardio group exhibits the smallest spread between baseline and fine-tuned variants at roughly 1.5 units.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the negative log-probability of clinically relevant tokens for the MistralV0.2-Base model and its variants fine-tuned on data from six medical specialties: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics. The x-axis represents the per-specialty terms, with each specialty group containing two bars: the baseline MistralV0.2-Base (light blue) and the model fine-tuned on that specialty’s data (colored according to the specialty). The y-axis shows the negative log probability, ranging from approximately -27 to -22, where lower values indicate stronger token predictions. Across all specialties, the baseline model consistently exhibits higher negative log probabilities (worse predictions) compared to the fine-tuned variants. The Gastro-tuned model achieves the lowest negative log probabilities in most categories, indicating strong performance and cross-specialty transferability. The Infect group shows the largest overall negative log probabilities, with the baseline reaching around -23.5, while the Cardio group displays the smallest difference between baseline and fine-tuned models, approximately 1.5 units, suggesting limited improvement from fine-tuning in this specialty.
